proofs.P08-api-health-and-static-security: The actual HTTP test confirms the health path stays public while project data requires authentication, and verifies CSP nonce replacement, safe hashed Vite asset serving, symlink rejection, and denial of arbitrary source files.
proofs.P08-api-profile-metadata: The version route reports this Scriptorium API and contracts version, selected profile, cookie-owner/bearer-read-compute-propose auth modes, runtime metadata, and current module availability; it does not return legacy Loom metadata.
proofs.P08-core-snapshot-actions: The HTTP boundary test verifies pinned tree/scene, manuscript snapshot list and historical body routes, bounded search and writing-stat envelopes, and composed Core action descriptors/results with input schema errors. Reads retain the selected Core snapshot identity.
proofs.P08-author-mutation-boundary: The HTTP boundary test verifies the host replaces request-supplied proposal provenance with `mcp` for bearer requests and MCP module contributions, allows declared compute under runtime effect limits, denies bearer approval, accepts same-origin owner-session approval with host-assigned owner scope, and exposes proposal review/status reads. Legacy direct scene PUT is retired with HTTP 410 so persistent scene changes use proposal, approval, and checkpoint routes.
proofs.P08-project-lifecycle: Owner-scoped project list, detail, and registration use CoreStore. PUT re-registration accepts only the stored canonical URL and the verified current default branch, then delegates reconstruction to Core; mismatched remotes and credentials/settings are rejected before Core runs. DELETE delegates to Core's guarded detach. A real local-bare-Git HTTP test confirms URL mismatch leaves both the clone and registry unchanged, Core reconstruction preserves the project, dirty-tree detach is refused, and clean detach removes the registration. PATCH returns a typed retirement response for legacy auto-merge settings. The owner event stream emits only actual started/completed/failed manual sync outcomes, with correlated sync and observation data, and closes on server shutdown.
proofs.P08-provider-none: The provider feature endpoint requires authentication and returns `providerKind: none` without preventing project, read, proposal, or review paths from operating.
proofs.P08-scratch-core-operation: The HTTP boundary test checks scratch text and bounded binary attachments are represented as Core change operations and sent through proposal/approval/checkpoint methods; no API-side project file writer is used.
proofs.P08-module-http-composition: The actual `ModuleRuntime` and Fastify-backed HTTP server test activate a lazy fixture module, dispatch its relative contribution path with a fresh remote reader, and enforce owner-only access on its owner route. Public contribution dispatch is covered with an in-memory registered remote reader.
proofs.P08-public-module-attenuation: The public module test verifies the handler gets a fresh remote reader, cannot invoke or enumerate composed actions or read linked repositories, receives no ambient cookie, bearer, or proxy-authorization headers, and can return only the explicitly allowed public Referrer-Policy and X-Robots-Tag headers. Runtime-side public-context rejection is implemented in P03.

compositionLimits: The source `/api/reload` rebuilt a derived SQLite projection. The target reads pinned Core snapshots and has no equivalent persistent author-data index to reload, so P08 does not expose a misleading reload endpoint; the final ledger still needs to record that projection maintenance disposition.

P08 API exposes generic module action and HTTP contribution adapters. MCP-specific HTTP/stdio tools, enabled-module domain actions, and the full browser review flow are owned by their module/UI tasks and require composed integration checks.

This evidence does not certify `start()` inside Core/full OCI profiles, real GitHub checkpoint/publish recovery, or container shutdown under a live streamed request. Those remain P13/P12 integration acceptance. The P08 API tests use in-memory runtime fixtures for several host boundaries and a real local bare-Git Core instance for project registration, reconstruction, and detach; the separate P13 publishing acceptance must run against the composed real Core/Fastify/runtime and authorized GitHub fixture.

The owner event stream reports manual sync requests handled by this API instance. It is not a cross-process/Core-wide event bus. Legacy auto-merge settings are explicitly retired by the fixed approval and publication workflow.
